arguments.prompt:
I need to understand the structure of the /app/a.out binary file to create a program that extracts memory values from it.

Please:
1. Check if /app/a.out exists and examine its properties
2. Use tools like `file`, `hexdump`, `xxd`, or `objdump` to understand the binary format
3. Look at the ELF header and section headers to understand what sections exist
4. Identify where the actual memory values might be stored (likely in .text, .data, .bss sections)
5. Provide details about:
   - The file type and architecture
   - Section names and their offsets/sizes
   - The raw bytes in each section

This is a read-only investigation - do not modify any files.

arguments.command: which xxd objdump hexdump readelf 2>/dev/null; ls -la /usr/bin/ | grep -E "(xxd|objdump|hexdump|readelf|file)" 2>/dev/null
readelf -S /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .data /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .rodata /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .text /app/a.out
readelf -x .init_array /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .fini_array /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .got /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .dynamic /app/a.out
readelf -x .plt /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .plt.got /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .plt.sec /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .eh_frame /app/a.out
readelf -x .interp /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .note.gnu.build-id /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .gnu.hash /app/a.out && echo "---" && readelf -x .dynsym /app/a.out
ls -la /app/ && cat /app/*.json 2>/dev/null || echo "No JSON files found"

node extract.js /app/a.out 2>&1 | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total entries: {len(d)}'); print('Sample entries:'); items=list(d.items())[:20]; print('\n'.join(f'{k}: {v}' for k,v in items))"
node extract.js /app/a.out 2>&1 | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'Total entries: {len(d)}'); items=list(d.items())[:30]; print('\n'.join(f'{k}: {v}' for k,v in items))"
